1.question: Where was Ezekiel when the heavens were opened and he saw visions of God (Ezekiel 1:1)?
options: In the midst of the congregation, in the temple court
Among the captives by the river of Chebar
In the court of king Nebuchadnezzar, in Babylon
Beside the altar, within the sanctuary

1.question: How many faces and wings did each of the four living creatures have (Ezekiel 1:6)?
options: Two faces and two wings
Four faces and four wings
One face and six wings
Three faces and four wings

1.question: According to Ezekiel 1:10, the four faces of each creature were the face of a man, a lion, an ox, and what?
options: An eagle
A serpent
A horse
A ram

1.question: What was beside the living creatures upon the earth in Ezekiel 1:15-16?
options: A pillar of cloud and fire that covered the whole camp of Israel
A wheel, as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel
A bronze altar surrounded by flames of burning fire all around
A wooden staff fixed firmly into the ground

1.title: Wheels full of eyes
1.text: The wheels are described as 'so high that they were dreadful' and their rings 'full of eyes round about' — an image of God's all-seeing presence that moves freely in every direction, even among captives far from the temple.

1.question: In Ezekiel 1:24 the noise of the creatures' wings was like what?
options: The sound of a mighty rushing wind sweeping across the desert
The roar of many chariots of war rushing forth to battle
The noise of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty
The sound of trumpets echoing far in the valley

1.question: When Ezekiel saw the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord (Ezekiel 1:28), what did he do?
options: He sang for joy
He hid in a cave
He fell upon his face
He ran to Jerusalem

2.question: By what title does the Lord repeatedly address Ezekiel, beginning in Ezekiel 2:1?
options: Son of man
Servant of the Lord
Prophet of Judah
Man of God

2.title: Sent to a rebellious house
2.text: God warns that Israel may not listen, yet sends Ezekiel anyway 'whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear' — the prophet's task is faithfulness, not guaranteed success.

2.template: there was written therein lamentations, and mourning, and {0}

2.question: What was written on the roll of a book shown to Ezekiel (Ezekiel 2:10)?
options: Promises of restoration and lasting peace
Lamentations, and mourning, and woe
Blessings and promises of great prosperity
The names of the twelve tribes of Israel

3.question: When Ezekiel ate the roll the Lord gave him, how did it taste (Ezekiel 3:3)?
options: Bland, with no flavor at all
As honey for sweetness
Salty like water from the sea
Spicy like hot pepper

3.question: To whom is Ezekiel sent to speak in Ezekiel 3:4-5?
options: To a people of a strange speech and hard language
To the house of Israel
To the kings of Babylon
To the priests of Egypt

3.question: What role does the Lord give Ezekiel for the house of Israel in Ezekiel 3:17?
options: A judge
A watchman
A king
A scribe

3.title: Seven days astonished
3.text: Before he could speak, Ezekiel sat among the captives at Tel-abib 'astonished' for seven days — overwhelmed by what he had seen before the word of the Lord came to him again.

3.question: Where did the Lord tell Ezekiel to go to speak with him in Ezekiel 3:22?
options: Into the plain
Up the mountain
To the temple
Across the river

3.question: According to Ezekiel 3:26, what would happen to Ezekiel's tongue?
options: It would be sent to preach before the strange nations
It would cleave to the roof of his mouth so he would be dumb
It would speak continually to rebuke the rebellious house
It would be strengthened to cry aloud in the streets

4.question: What city was Ezekiel told to portray upon the tile in Ezekiel 4:1?
options: Babylon
Jerusalem
Nineveh
Samaria

4.question: How many days was Ezekiel to lie on his left side, bearing the iniquity of Israel (Ezekiel 4:5)?
options: Two hundred and ninety-five days
Three hundred sixty-five days
Three hundred and ninety days
One hundred twenty-five days

4.title: A day for a year
4.text: The Lord tells Ezekiel, 'I have appointed thee each day for a year' (4:6) — the days he lies on each side stand for the years of Israel's and Judah's guilt, turning his body into a living calendar of judgment.

4.question: How was Ezekiel to measure the food he ate during the sign (Ezekiel 4:10)?
options: By weight, twenty shekels a day
By measure, ten cubits of water each day
Only in the morning and at evening time
With no restriction on the weight at all

4.question: Why would the people of Jerusalem eat bread by weight and drink water by measure (Ezekiel 4:16-17)?
options: So that an ancient covenant made with the neighboring kings before the captivity would be fulfilled
Because the Lord would break the staff of bread, so they would consume away for their iniquity
Because a foreign prophet had pronounced a curse upon the city and all its inhabitants who dwelt within its walls
So that the people would learn to cultivate new crops during the long coming winter season

5.question: What sign act did the Lord command Ezekiel to perform with a sharp knife in Ezekiel 5:1?
options: Build a grand altar of stones before all the people
Shave his head and his beard, then divide the hair
Dig a great pit deep in the middle of the besieged city
Sacrifice a young lamb upon an altar of stone

5.question: Why does the Lord say he will not spare Jerusalem in Ezekiel 5:11?
options: Because she defiled his sanctuary with detestable things and abominations
Because she was too small to resist the armies of the neighboring nations
Because of a great famine that ravaged the whole land for many long years
Because she trusted in alliances with Egypt instead of trusting the Lord

5.title: Set in the midst of the nations
5.text: The Lord says of Jerusalem, 'This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations' (5:5). Chosen to be an example of righteousness to the surrounding peoples, she instead exceeded them in wickedness.

5.question: Which judgments does the Lord say he will send upon Jerusalem in Ezekiel 5:12,17?
options: Earthquake, thunder, hail, and fire from heaven upon the city
Famine, evil beasts, pestilence, blood, and the sword
Darkness, locusts, frogs, and blood upon the rivers of the land
Pestilence, famine, and fiery rain from heaven

6.question: Against what does the Lord tell Ezekiel to set his face and prophesy in Ezekiel 6:2-3?
options: The mountains of Israel
The ships of Tyre
The rivers of Egypt
The walls of Babylon

6.title: Against the high places
6.text: The 'high places' (6:3) were hilltop shrines where Israel offered to idols. By turning the judgment against the very mountains, the Lord strikes at the heart of the nation's idolatry.

6.question: What did the Lord say the escaped remnant would do among the nations (Ezekiel 6:9-10)?
options: Forget the Lord entirely and worship new idols of all the nations
Remember the Lord and loathe themselves for their abominations
Make war on Babylon in order to win back their freedom and land
Build temples to the idols they had brought from the nations

6.question: By what three things does Ezekiel 6:11-12 say the house of Israel shall fall?
options: By war, by plague, and by complete total destruction
By the sword, the famine, and the pestilence
By famine, by pestilence, and by utter ruin of the cities
By pestilence and by war alone forever

7.question: What single word does the Lord repeatedly declare has come upon the land of Israel in Ezekiel 7:2-3?
options: The end
The dawn
The harvest
The feast

7.title: An end, not just a siege
7.text: Earlier chapters warned of siege; here the message sharpens to a final reckoning — 'An end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land' (7:2). The day of the Lord's wrath has arrived for Israel.

7.question: In Ezekiel 7:10, what is said to have blossomed and budded as the day comes?
options: The wrath and the vengeance
The rod and pride
The violence and the terror
The root and the fruit

7.question: According to Ezekiel 7:15, where are the sword, the pestilence, and the famine?
options: The pestilence and famine are without, and the sword is within
The sword is without, and the pestilence and the famine within
The sword and the pestilence are within, and the famine is without
Only outside the city will the sword be found there

7.question: Into whose hands will the Lord give the land for a prey and a spoil in Ezekiel 7:21?
options: The priests and the princes of the land of Judah
The armies of Egypt and of the great Assyria
The strangers and the wicked of the earth
The destroying angels of the Lord

7.question: According to Ezekiel 7:26, when the people seek a vision of the prophet, what will be lacking?
options: The word of the prophet and the blessing of the great kings
The law from the priest and counsel from the ancients
The vision of the seer and the counsel from the scribes
Bread from the baker and wine from the farmer

8.question: To what city was Ezekiel carried in the visions of God in Ezekiel 8:3?
options: Babylon
Jerusalem
Bethel
Tyre

8.title: The image of jealousy
8.text: At the temple gate Ezekiel sees 'the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy' (8:3) — an idol set up in God's own house, the first of a tour of escalating abominations within the sanctuary.

8.question: When Ezekiel dug in the wall as the Lord told him in Ezekiel 8:7-8, what did he find?
options: A buried treasure
A door
A hidden spring
A scroll

8.question: How many men of the ancients of Israel stood with censers before the idols, and who was among them (Ezekiel 8:11)?
options: Fifty men, with Hezekiah the son of great Hilkiah
Seventy men, with Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan
Thirty-five men, with Baruch the son of Neriah
Twelve men, with Korah the son of Levi

8.question: How does the Lord say he will respond to these abominations in Ezekiel 8:18?
options: He will show compassion; he will heed their cries and grant them mercy, favor, and rest
He will deal in fury; his eye shall not spare, and though they cry he will not hear
He will delay judgment for many years and send prophets to call them all to repentance
He will forgive at once and quickly restore the glory of the temple

9.template: one man among them was clothed with {0}

9.question: What was the man clothed with linen told to set upon the foreheads of certain men in Ezekiel 9:4?
options: A crown of gold, upon those who kept faithfully the law
A mark, upon those who sigh and cry for the abominations
A holy oil, upon the priests who faithfully served at the altar
A red mark, upon the elders who judged the people

9.title: Begin at my sanctuary
9.text: The Lord commands the slayers to spare those who bear the mark but to 'begin at my sanctuary' (9:6) — judgment starts with God's own house and its corrupt leaders before reaching the city.

9.question: What did the man clothed with linen report when he returned in Ezekiel 9:11?
options: That the whole city had already been rebuilt
That he had done as he was commanded
That all the wicked had fled far away
That the people had repented in their hearts

10.question: What did the Lord tell the man clothed with linen to fill his hands with and scatter over the city (Ezekiel 10:2)?
options: Seeds scattered upon the altars of the temple
Coals of fire from between the cherubims
Pure water drawn out from the river Chebar
Pure incense from the golden altar

10.title: The glory leaves the threshold
10.text: In 10:4 'the glory of the Lord went up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house' — a step in the slow, sorrowful departure of God's presence from the temple before its destruction.

10.question: How are the wheels described in Ezekiel 10:9-10?
options: As four separate wheels, each one turned toward a different side
As a wheel in the midst of a wheel, all of one likeness
As great wheels of stone, fixed and held forever to the ground
As small wooden wheels, hidden within the wall

10.question: Which four faces did each cherub have, according to Ezekiel 10:14?
options: Cherub, man, lion, and eagle
Lamb, ox, dove, and serpent
Man, horse, ram, and fish
Lion, bear, leopard, and goat

10.question: As what does Ezekiel identify the cherubims in Ezekiel 10:15,20?
options: Angels that had never appeared to him before that very day
The living creatures he had seen by the river of Chebar
The seraphim who always served before the heavenly throne
Ancient statues from the holy place of the temple

11.question: What proverb did the princes of the people say in Ezekiel 11:3?
options: This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh
This people is the vine, and we are the clusters
This land is the great oven, and we the bread
This wall is the fortress, and we the stones

11.title: Named leaders
11.text: Ezekiel names the princes at the gate — Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah (11:1) — concrete leaders held responsible for the wicked counsel given in the city.

11.question: What did the Lord say would happen to those who trusted the 'caldron' in Ezekiel 11:8-10?
options: They would be crowned as princes and receive a great blessing of Israel
He would bring a sword upon them and judge them in the border of Israel
They would prosper greatly in the streets and be free from any judgment at all
They would flee safely to Egypt with all their possessions

11.question: In Ezekiel 11:15, what had the inhabitants of Jerusalem said to Ezekiel's brethren in exile?
options: Come back at once into the city: the Lord has already forgiven all sins
Get you far from the Lord: unto us is this land given in possession
Bring us gold and fine silver from Babylon for the temple of the Lord
Pray always for our king and for the lasting peace of the city

11.question: What new thing does the Lord promise to give in Ezekiel 11:19?
options: A new temple of pure gold, built in the midst of Jerusalem to endure through all generations
One heart and a new spirit, taking away the stony heart and giving a heart of flesh
A new king from the lineage of David, who would reign forever over all the nations of the earth
A new law written on tablets of stone, given to all the people of Israel

11.question: Where did the glory of the Lord go and what did Ezekiel then do (Ezekiel 11:23-25)?
options: It filled the whole temple with great glory, and he sang out joyful praises before all the assembled people
It went up from the city to the mountain on the east, and he told the captives all the Lord had shown him
It returned once more to Mount Sinai, and he slept extremely deeply for seven long and weary days and nights
It vanished suddenly, and he wept quietly in silence throughout the whole dark night

12.question: What sign act does the Lord command Ezekiel to perform in Ezekiel 12:3-5?
options: Shave his head and beard, then divide the hair into three parts, and burn one part
Prepare baggage for removing, dig through the wall, and go forth as into captivity
Lie upon his left side before all the people continually for many long days and nights
Raise a standard upon the mountain and blow the trumpet at early dawn

12.title: Eyes that see not
12.text: The Lord describes Israel as a rebellious house 'which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not' (12:2) — so Ezekiel must act out his message in plain sight to break through their blindness.

12.question: Whom does the 'burden' of Ezekiel 12:10 concern?
options: The prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel
The rebellious elders who dwelt in the land of Moab
The king of Tyre and his merchants from the isles of the sea
The false prophets who dwelt in the city of Samaria

12.question: What does the Lord say the people will know when he scatters them among the nations (Ezekiel 12:15)?
options: That the prophets were false
That I am the Lord
That Babylon is mighty
That the land is cursed

12.question: With what was Ezekiel told to eat his bread and drink his water in Ezekiel 12:18?
options: With songs of praise and great rejoicing
With quaking and trembling and carefulness
In complete silence, without looking at anyone
Kneeling, turned toward the temple

12.question: How does the Lord answer the saying that 'every vision faileth' in Ezekiel 12:23,25,28?
options: He explains that the visions were only meant for the ancient days and shall no longer apply now
He declares that none of his words shall be prolonged, but shall come to pass without delay
He promises to reveal new visions only after Jerusalem has been completely and fully rebuilt
He commands the prophets to keep silent until the time of the new king arrives

13.title: Foxes among the ruins
13.text: Verse 4 likens Israel's false prophets to "foxes in the deserts" — scavengers that burrow into broken walls rather than repair them, a vivid charge against leaders who exploit ruin instead of mending it.

13.question: In Ezekiel 13:5, what had the false prophets failed to do?
options: Go up into the gaps and make up the hedge for the house of Israel
Warn the people of their sins and call them to true repentance before the Lord
Intercede before the Lord for the captives carried away to Babylon
Rebuild the temple destroyed by the Chaldean armies

13.question: What false message had the prophets given the people, according to Ezekiel 13:10?
options: Safety forevermore throughout the land
Peace, when there was no peace
Great victory over the army of Babylon
Blessings without measure

13.template: Say unto them which daub it with {0} mortar

13.question: In Ezekiel 13:16, what did these prophets of Israel see for Jerusalem?
options: Visions of great future prosperity for the people
A deliverer sent by the Lord against the Chaldeans
Visions of peace, when there was no peace
Signs of divine blessing ahead

13.question: What does the Lord promise in Ezekiel 13:23 about the false prophets' power?
options: They shall be restored to the congregation and honored as leaders
They shall receive greater power to prophesy in the Lord's name
They shall be sent to prophesy among the nations
They shall see no more vanity nor divine divinations

14.question: Why do the elders who come to Ezekiel receive no true answer from the Lord (Ezekiel 14:3-4)?
options: They have set up their idols in their heart
They refused to fast before coming into the prophet's presence
They still kept a secret covenant with the king of Egypt
They doubted Ezekiel's prophetic authority

14.question: According to Ezekiel 14:6, what does the Lord command the house of Israel to do?
options: Gather in solemn fasting before the ruined temple
Repent and turn from their idols
Send messengers to make a covenant with the Chaldeans
Keep silent until the wrath had passed

14.question: Which three righteous men does Ezekiel 14:14 name, who could deliver only their own souls?
options: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Moses, Aaron, and Samuel
Noah, Daniel, and Job
Elijah, Elisha, and Isaiah

14.question: What are the Lord's "four sore judgments" upon Jerusalem in Ezekiel 14:21?
options: The captivity, the leprosy, the betrayal, and the forced exile
Civil war, enslavement, consuming fire, and destroying hail
The darkness, the silence, and the total confusion
The sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence

14.title: Daniel among the ancients
14.text: By naming Daniel beside Noah and Job as a byword for righteousness (v. 14), Ezekiel — a contemporary — treats Daniel, then a young exile in Babylon, as already famed for his integrity.

15.title: The useless vine wood
15.text: Unlike oak or cedar, a vine's wood is too crooked and soft to build with; its only worth is its fruit. The Lord's question in verse 2 sets up the whole point: a fruitless vine is good for nothing but burning.

15.question: In Ezekiel 15:4, what becomes of the vine wood once it is cast into the fire?
options: The wood turns to ashes that fertilize the vineyard soil
The fire devours both ends and the midst is burned
It is carefully kept to serve as firewood upon the temple altar
It becomes strong and is used to build doors

16.question: In the allegory of Ezekiel 16:6, what does the Lord say to the abandoned newborn?
options: Live
Flee
Be silent
Arise and walk

16.template: I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with {0} skin

16.question: According to Ezekiel 16:14, what made Jerusalem's renown go forth among the nations?
options: Her secret alliance with the kings of Egypt and Assyria
Her beauty, made perfect through the Lord's comeliness
The gold and silver brought as tribute from neighboring nations
Her military victories against the Philistines

16.question: Whom does Ezekiel 16:3 name as Jerusalem's symbolic father and mother?
options: An Egyptian and a Moabite
A Babylonian and a Philistine
An Amorite and a Hittite
An Assyrian and a Canaanite

16.question: In Ezekiel 16:27, into whose will did the Lord deliver Jerusalem when she went astray?
options: The daughters of the Moabites and Ammonites
The neighboring kings of all Israel
The armies of the land of Egypt
The daughters of the Philistines

16.title: Forgetting the day of rescue
16.text: The repeated charge (vv. 22) is that Jerusalem "hast not remembered the days of thy youth" — the heart of the allegory is ingratitude: forgetting the One who rescued and adorned her.

16.question: In Ezekiel 16:32, to what is unfaithful Jerusalem compared?
options: A servant who abandons her master to follow strangers
A wife that taketh strangers instead of her husband
An unfaithful wife who takes gifts instead of loving her husband
An unfaithful servant who trades masters for money

16.question: What does Ezekiel 16:35 call Jerusalem as it summons her to hear the word of the Lord?
options: O harlot
O daughter
O city
O Zion

16.question: According to Ezekiel 16:38, how will the Lord judge Jerusalem?
options: As rebellious kings against the Lord are severely judged
As women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged
As priests who defile the holy sanctuary are severely punished
As false prophets in all Israel are judged

16.question: What proverb does Ezekiel 16:44 say will be used against Jerusalem?
options: A prophet has no honor at home
Pride goeth before a fall
As is the mother, so is her daughter
The fathers have eaten sour grapes

16.question: In Ezekiel 16:46, who are named as Jerusalem's elder and younger sisters?
options: Babylon and Tyre
Nineveh and Damascus
Egypt and Edom
Samaria and Sodom

options: Pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness
Idolatry, bloodshed, and cruel oppression of the poor
Adultery, false witness, and worship of foreign idols
Violence, theft, and shedding of innocent blood

16.question: Despite the judgment, what does the Lord promise in Ezekiel 16:60?
options: To remember his covenant and establish an everlasting covenant
To raise up a magnificent new temple in Jerusalem for all eternity
To send mighty armies to quickly restore the whole kingdom of Judah
To immediately forgive all the wickedness of Jerusalem

17.question: In the riddle of Ezekiel 17:3, what does the great eagle take from Lebanon?
options: The highest branch of the cedar
The deepest root of the whole vine
The entire trunk of the Lebanon cedar
The lower branches of the olive tree

17.question: What did the seed of the land become after it was planted, in Ezekiel 17:6?
options: A tall and leafy cedar planted on the mountain
A spreading vine of low stature
A fruitful tree of great height and shade
A wide field of ripening wheat

17.question: How does Ezekiel 17:12 interpret the riddle of the first eagle?
options: The Pharaoh of Egypt sending his armies to rescue Judah from its enemies
The king of Assyria invading the northern kingdom and carrying its people captive
The king of Babylon coming to Jerusalem and taking its king and princes
The high priest defiling the temple with pagan sacrifices

17.question: According to Ezekiel 17:15, against whom did the vine-king rebel by sending ambassadors to Egypt?
options: Against Assyria
Against the Philistines
Against the Ammonites
Against the king of Babylon

17.title: The tender twig on the high mountain
17.text: After all the judgment, verse 22 turns hopeful: the Lord himself will crop a tender shoot from the high cedar's top and plant it on a high and eminent mountain — long read as a messianic promise that the Lord will raise up the kingdom he chooses.

17.question: What does the Lord declare he does in Ezekiel 17:24, that all the trees of the field may know?
options: He brings down the high tree and exalts the low tree
He dries up the green tree and makes the dry tree flourish
He plants new cedars on every mountain across Israel
He sends fire upon all the trees of the field

options: He shall surely live
He shall be made a king
He shall be rich
He shall never sorrow

18.question: In Ezekiel 18:13, what is said of the violent son who does all these abominations?
options: He shall be quickly forgiven because his father intercedes for him
He shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him
He shall live forever because of his father's righteousness

18.question: According to Ezekiel 18:17, does the righteous son die for the iniquity of his wicked father?
options: Yes, he fully carries all the guilt of his father
He dies together with his father because of the wickedness

18.question: What proverb does the Lord forbid Israel to use, in Ezekiel 18:2-3?
options: The son bears the father's iniquity, and the father bears the son's iniquity

18.question: In Ezekiel 18:21, what happens to the wicked who turns from all his sins?
options: He shall surely live; he shall not die
He still surely dies for all his former sins
He must offer sacrifices before being forgiven

18.question: What complaint does Israel raise in Ezekiel 18:25, which the Lord answers?
options: The way of the Lord is not equal
The Lord no longer hears our prayers
The sins of the fathers fall upon the children
God has abandoned his chosen people

18.title: A new heart and a new spirit
18.text: Verse 31's plea — "make you a new heart and a new spirit" — anticipates the promise of Ezekiel 36 to replace the heart of stone with a heart of flesh; here it is framed as something the people are urged to do.

18.question: How does Ezekiel 18:32 describe the Lord's desire toward the one who dies?
options: He greatly delights in the judgment of the wicked
He has no pleasure in the death of him that dieth
He remains completely indifferent to human suffering
He greatly rejoices in the punishment of the rebellious

19.question: In the lamentation of Ezekiel 19:2, to what is the mother of the princes compared?
options: A lioness lying down among lions
An eagle soaring over the high rocky cliffs
A vine flourishing beside abundant waters
A gentle ewe among a scattered flock

19.question: What became of the first young lion, according to Ezekiel 19:4?
options: He was captured by neighboring armies and led away to the land of Assyria
He was taken in their pit and brought with chains to Egypt
He was mortally wounded in battle and buried in the mountains of Israel
He fled into the wilderness and lived hidden among the rocks

19.title: From lions to a withered vine
19.text: The poem shifts its figure midway: the princes are first young lions caught by the nations, then a fruitful vine plucked up and dried by the east wind — a double image of Judah's fallen royal house.

20.question: In Ezekiel 20:6, how does the Lord describe the land he swore to bring Israel into?
options: Flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands
A dry and arid land, without water or any shade
A land of great cities fortified with high walls
A narrow valley surrounded by steep rocky cliffs

20.question: What did the Lord give Israel in the wilderness, by which a man should live, in Ezekiel 20:11?
options: A covenant written on tablets of stone
His statutes and judgments
A new name and a new lineage
Water from the rock in the desert

20.question: According to Ezekiel 20:21, what did the children do, like their fathers?
options: They built foreign altars upon the sacred mountains
They offered their firstborn children to idols
They rebelled and polluted the sabbaths
They forgot the judgments given in the wilderness

20.question: In Ezekiel 20:27, in what further way does the Lord say Israel's fathers had blasphemed him?
options: By committing a trespass against him
By raising pagan altars upon every high hill
By sacrificing their children to the foreign god Molech
By refusing to keep the solemn feasts

20.question: In Ezekiel 20:32, what did Israel say in their mind that shall not come to pass?
options: We will be as the heathen, to serve wood and stone
We will return to Egypt and serve their gods again
We will be exalted above all the nations of the whole earth
We will no longer be afflicted by our enemies

20.question: What does the Lord say he will do in Ezekiel 20:37 as he gathers his people?
options: Cause them to pass under the rod and bring them into the bond of the covenant
He will send his angels to gather the scattered tribes throughout all the nations of the earth
